plan: In a second-price auction, bidding your true value is a weakly dominant strategy regardless of the number of competitors or their bidding behavior. Since I win only if I have the highest bid and pay the second-highest bid, bidding exactly my value ensures I capture all profitable opportunities (winning whenever my value exceeds the second-highest bid) while never overpaying. With a value of $48, I will bid my true value to maximize expected profit.

In a second-price auction, the dominant strategy is to bid your true value, since you pay the second-highest bid (not your own bid) if you win. My value for this item is $0, meaning I have nothing to gain from winning - I would only lose money if I won since I'd have to pay whatever the second-highest bid is while gaining $0 in value. Therefore, I should bid exactly $0 to avoid any risk of winning and losing money.

In a second-price sealed-bid auction, bidding your true value is a dominant strategy regardless of the number of bidders or their strategies. This is because you pay the second-highest bid (not your own), so bidding above value risks overpaying, and bidding below value risks losing profitable opportunities. With my value at $14, I should bid exactly $14 to maximize expected profit, as this ensures I win whenever profitable and pay the correct competitive price.
